recipe.label: Ceramic Mosaic

traits.medium: hand-set ceramic-mosaic-looking interpretation of a sunset seascape
traits.texture: small irregular glazed tile-like shapes separated by fine matte grout
traits.composition: tile groups follow the large cloud bands, dark island horizon and rippling-water rhythm
traits.lighting: subtle glints on tiles while retaining the original sunset light structure

review_checks: cloud and reflection bands remain readable
limitations: No tile schedule, fabrication pattern, seamless texture or exact tessellation is supplied.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Ceramic Mosaic example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A wide view across dark gently rippling water toward low island silhouettes beneath an expansive sunset sky. The horizon sits low, with a larger dark headland at the left edge, layered orange, coral, gold and purple clouds and a tiny distant boat near the right horizon.
Style/medium: hand-set ceramic-mosaic-looking interpretation of a sunset seascape
Color palette: #E6C76B, #CA7557, #956D85, #38515A, #E9DFCC
Materials/textures: small irregular glazed tile-like shapes separated by fine matte grout
Composition/framing: tile groups follow the large cloud bands, dark island horizon and rippling-water rhythm; Keep landscape orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: subtle glints on tiles while retaining the original sunset light structure
Requested output target: 1536x1024, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original low horizon, open water, dark left headland, low islands and sweeping layered sunset clouds. The sky dominates. Do not add a garden, terrace, trees or a towering central cloud.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
